title: The Remaining Role of Humans in the “Human World” — M.L. Luesak Chakrabandhu

Luesak Chakrabandhu In an era where AI and machines are so capable that they can perform tasks and make decisions on behalf of humans in almost every matter, if we still want this to remain a “human world” in which humans hold the ultimate power to control and determine its direction, we must preserve three core roles. First — “The Consumer” Humans remain the users of resources and the beneficiaries of the economic system, even if in the future machines produce goods, provide services, and create almost all economic value. Human consumption therefore remains a key reason why the economic system of the “human world” continues to exist. Second — “The Responsible Party” Not merely the “person in charge” of the work, but the “person held liable” when problems or damage arise from a system to which humans have delegated authority. Machines or AI do not fear punishment the way humans do. Deleting an AI or dismantling a robot does not carry the same meaning as punishing a human, nor does it guarantee that the problem will not recur. Therefore, humans must remain responsible for the critical mechanisms and possess sufficient authority to oversee those systems. The Third — “The System Tuner” Humans must not merely retain the power to approve or issue commands; they must possess sufficient knowledge, understanding, and morality to actually design, adjust, and control various systems. These three roles are what humans must uphold , especially in setting the rules and controlling resource, energy, and safety systems. If we allow AI to alter the systems without human understanding or control, we may lose the power to determine the future of the “human world.” If you are interested in the details of this concept, you can read the full article here , and I have also presented this idea formally at the AI & IoT Summit 2026 — Open Source AI .
